weather_report:
Midday in Perth arrives with a quilt of broken cloud, sunlight slipping through in bright, gentle pulses. It feels like a day that never quite makes up its mind, yet the air is clear and the view to the horizon remains clean. Expect the pattern to hold through the afternoon into early evening: intervals of warm brightness, then a softer, muted light as the cloud drifts across. Even with the cloud, the sun still bites at this time of year, and the UV will be strong around lunchtime; it’s the kind of day where a hat, sunglasses, and a good lick of sunscreen are more useful than a jacket.

Dress for ease: breathable fabrics, light layers you can shrug on if a passing shadow cools the moment. It’s pleasant enough to take lunch on a shaded veranda, run a few errands on foot while the sun ducks in and out, or peg the washing where it can drink the shifting light. Keep the longer jaunt for later in the day when the glare eases—an unhurried loop along the river, or a quiet wander under the first purple bells of jacaranda-lined streets, then home to a chair by an open window and the low hum of the afternoon.
